title: Leaving Young over going to Texas; joining Art Bronson in Salina
summary: The band ran from December 1926 to January 1928; the men did not want to go South, Lester quit in Salina and Phillips and Jones followed, all joining Art Bronson in January 1928.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So you started playing with them in Minneapolis in '27 was it?
'26. Fall of '26, around December.
December 1926. How long did you play with that band?
I played with that band until we quit and went with Art Bronson. That was in '28.
What part of '28 was that?
December.
So that band played all the way from December of '26 to January of '28.
Yeah.
Then in January of '28 what happened?
In January of '28, he was going down in Texas, and we decided we didn't want to go down in Texas. So Les, he quit in Salina, Kansas.
You said you guys didn't want to go down to Texas.
No, we didn't want to go down to Texas.
I had heard that Lester didn't want to go down to the South because the racial prejudice was so bad down there.
Yeah, well, that's the reason we all didn't want to go. So Les quit in Salina, but me and Pete stayed
Phillips - 76

with him until he got to Wichita, and we quit in Wichita. We went back to Salina where Les was. And Bronson was in Salina. That's where Bronson was. He had six pieces, and he wanted to get a 10-piece band together.
So this is January 1928.
Yeah. So when we came in town, he was glad to get us, you know what I mean?
So who all were you again? It was Lester, you, Pete Jones...
Three of us. That's when we got with Bronson, in Salina, Kansas, January 1928. Then I stayed with Bronson up to 1931.
